title: Tiwanaku was the capital of an Andean power before the Inca
body: Tiwanaku, in what is now Bolivia, reached its height between about 500 and 900 CE. The surviving stone monuments belong to a civilisation that held influence across much of the southern Andes.
takeaway: The Andes had several centres of political power across its history, separated by centuries.
visual: large fitted stone blocks and a weathered gateway on the Bolivian altiplano

title: Uruguay's Fray Bentos exported preserved meat to Europe
body: At Fray Bentos, a factory founded in 1859 processed cattle from Uruguay's prairies. Meat extract and corned beef went to European buyers from 1865, and frozen meat was exported from 1924.
takeaway: Changing how food was preserved widened the choice of goods a distant factory could sell.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape (2015)
visual: a brick riverside factory with old loading equipment on its quay
